title: Waste, Recycling & Broken Glass
blurb: Safe waste handling: never put your hand in a bin, deal with broken glass properly and sort waste correctly.

Where each waste stream goes: general, mixed recycling, glass and used cooking oil
Where the brush and dustpan, and the ice scoop, are kept behind the bar

cards.title: Waste, Recycling & Broken Glass
cards.body:
By the end of this session you can:
- never put your hand into a bin
- deal with broken glass safely
- sort waste into the right streams

cards.title: Safety and the environment
cards.body: Handling waste is a daily job, and doing it well matters for two reasons: safety and the environment. Bins hide sharp and broken items, waste attracts pests if it is not managed, and sorting it correctly helps cut what goes to landfill.

cards.title: Never put your hand into a bin
cards.body: You cannot see what is in there. A hidden piece of broken glass, a knife or a skewer can cause a deep cut. If something needs pushing down, use a tool, not your hand.

left.title: Do
items: Use a tool to push waste down

right.title: Do not
items: Put your hand in a bin
Overfill so sharp things stick out of the top

cards.title: Never with bare hands
cards.body: Broken glass deserves special care. Behind the bar, breakages happen fast.

items.title: Clear and warn
items.text: Clear the area and warn people.

items.title: Sweep
items.text: Brush and dustpan, never bare hands.

items.title: Glass bin
items.text: Designated broken-glass bin or labelled sturdy container, not general waste.

cards.title: Ice and glass
cards.body: Never use a glass to scoop ice. Glass breaks fast, and the pieces end up in the ice.

left.title: Do
items: Clear the area and warn people

right.title: Do not
items: Use a glass to scoop ice
Pick up broken glass by hand

cards.title: Sort it
cards.body: Sort waste into the correct streams. Keep bin areas clean and lids closed to deter pests. Small habits from everyone add up to a safer, greener venue.

items: Used cooking oil in its own container

cards.title: Remember
cards.body:
- Never put your hand into a bin, use a tool
- Do not overfill bins
- Broken glass: brush and dustpan, wrap it, broken-glass bin
- Never use a glass to scoop ice
- Sort waste, used cooking oil never down the drain, lids closed

cards.q: You should never put your hand into a bin.
cards.why: You cannot see what is in there, and hidden glass, a knife or a skewer can cause a deep cut.

cards.q: How should you deal with broken glass?
options: Pick it up carefully with a bar cloth
Brush and dustpan, then the broken-glass bin
Push it under the counter until service ends
Wipe it into the general bin with a bar towel
cards.why: Never use bare hands. Sweep it up, wrap it and put it in the designated broken-glass bin or container.

cards.q: If something needs pushing down in a bin, use…
cards.why: Use a tool, not your hand.

cards.q: Broken glass can go in with the general waste.
cards.why: Broken glass goes in the designated broken-glass bin or a labelled sturdy container, separate from general waste.
Used cooking oil goes into its proper container and never down the drain.

cards.q: You should never use a glass to scoop ice.
cards.why: Glass breaks fast behind the bar. Never use a glass to scoop ice.

cards.q: Why is overfilling a bin a hazard?
options: It makes the bin much harder to lift
It makes the bin area smell worse
Sharp items stick out and cause cuts
It takes longer to sort the recycling
cards.why: Never overfill bins so that sharp things stick out of the top.

cards.q: Sorting waste correctly helps cut what goes to landfill.
cards.why: Sorting waste into the correct streams helps cut what goes to landfill.
Keep bin areas clean and lids closed to deter pests.

cards.q: Bins can hide sharp items you cannot see.
cards.why: A bin can hide broken glass, knives and skewers, which is why you never put your hand in.
